schema_version.description: Format version of the report DOCUMENT envelope (meta/summary/groups/findings), independent of meta.version (the panopticon release) and meta.ocrdb_version. Optional for back-compat: legacy pre-5.1 reports omit it and read as version 0. #run7 DAT-F2A.

meta.description: #1602 ruling 4: CLOSED. `additionalProperties: false`, so a meta section the schema does not describe fails validation at RUN time, not only in tests/test_schema_parity.py -- which is how `host_capabilities` drifted for a whole release. Three producers write here and only three: `synth.report.assemble` (every section below except the four that follow), `synth.render.write_report` (`parts`, `discarded_claims_file`, `discarded_claims_count`) and `synth.report.attach_schema_status` (`schema_errors`). A new key means a schema entry in the same PR -- describe it, do not reopen this.

gate_security_mode.description: The security mode used by this report's gate, derived only from the controller-carried --security flag (standard when omitted). Unlike meta.security_mode, this never falls back to target-written groups.json. Absent on older reports.

parts.description: Basenames of the `<stem>_partN.json` continuation files this report was split into, written when the document exceeds the writer's byte budget. The main file then carries only the first chunk of `findings`, so a consumer that reads it alone has a PARTIAL report: hydrate the union before validating or comparing (synth/render._read_json_report is that reader).

discarded_claims_file.description: #15: basename of the `<stem>-discarded.json` sibling holding `discarded_claims` when the report is too large to carry them inline (rejected claims keep their full advisor prose and grow precisely when verification works well). Present only on a split report, and independent of `parts` -- the spill can happen with no findings chunking at all.

discarded_claims_count.description: #15: how many claims went to `discarded_claims_file`, so a reader of the main file alone still knows the size of what it is not holding.

schema_errors.description: #1639 P15: how many validation errors the PRE-WRITE pass (`synth.report.validate_report`: the published schema plus the domain rules the schema cannot express) raised against this report. Stamped after that pass, so it is in the artifact on disk but was not in the document that was validated. It is not the run's whole answer and must not be read as one: the artifact pass that follows re-validates the hydrated split union and the X0X sibling, which this count cannot include, and the `artifact invalid: N schema errors` status line carries that full count. Every artifact is still written either way -- a report that failed validation is on disk, with this count in it, precisely so it can be inspected.

tools.description: What the scanner layer meant for this run's REVIEWERS (#1637 P08) -- distinct from meta.coverage, which accounts for what the adapters produced.

panels_with_scanner_context.description: How many review panels were dispatched with tool output already on disk (`with`) and how many were not (`without`). Recorded per cell at the moment its prompt was rendered, so a run whose tool scan skipped cannot read like one that scanned. Both zero means no panel was dispatched at all.

disabled_mid_run.description: True when this run started with the tool scan enabled and had it switched off with --no-tools while in flight (#1637 P08) -- the non-destructive rescue from a scanner environment that moved after the scouts were paid for. Distinct from a run that never had tools at all, and stated on every report (false included) so its absence cannot be read as its not having been measured.

network.description: What egress each scanner was given this run, per tool, copied off `tools-manifest.json` (#1645). `none` is the `--network none` containers -- every scanner but the two ONLINE_ONLY adapters. `proxied:<comma-separated hosts>` is an ONLINE_ONLY adapter that ran on a per-run `--internal` network behind a deny-by-default forward proxy allowing exactly those advisory endpoints; before this it got Docker's DEFAULT BRIDGE, i.e. every service reachable from the runner's network. `excluded:<reason>` is one whose egress could not be established: it did NOT run and did NOT fall back to the bridge, and it rides the manifest's `excluded_scope` rather than `selected`. `{}` on a run with no tools manifest, or one written without the scan loop ever running: nothing was measured, which is not the same claim as nothing was granted. The manifest is target-writable, so `synth.repair.repair_tools_network` normalizes it to the types pinned here at the read (a malformed row costs a warning and the row, never the run) and bounds the block to 200 rows of at most 200 characters each, the same caps the `sanitized` block beside it is held to at the same boundary.

sanitized.description: What an adapter refused to hand its scanner, per adapter, copied off `tools-manifest.json` (#1646). pip-audit is given a GENERATED requirements file holding only bare PEP 508 lines, because resolving an editable/local/VCS/URL requirement runs the reviewed repository's PEP 517 build backend -- so the dependency audit can be PARTIAL, and this says by how much and which lines. `{}` on a run with no tools manifest: nothing was measured, which is not the same claim as nothing was dropped. The manifest is target-writable, so `synth.repair.repair_tools_sanitized` normalizes it to the types pinned here at the read (a malformed row costs a warning and the row, never the run) and bounds it to 200 rows of at most 200 characters each -- at the READ, because the manifest this guards against is one a target pre-committed and never passed through the producer that caps the controller's own.

source.description: The repo-relative manifest the lines came from (`requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`). Relative, never absolute: the report is published and an absolute path would carry the scanner host's layout into it. A candidate manifest that resolved OUTSIDE the target -- a symlinked `requirements.txt` -- is treated as absent and named here as `<name> outside target`, so a repo whose manifest escapes the tree cannot read like a repo that has none.

kept.description: How many lines were audited -- the size of the generated file the scanner was actually given.

dropped.description: One row per line that was NOT audited. URL credentials are masked at the producer (scripts.tools.pip_audit), because these lines are target-authored text.

line.description: The line as evaluated: `\` continuations joined, comments and `--hash=` tokens removed, credentials masked.

reason.description: Why it could not be audited. One of: `editable`; `local path`; `archive name` (a bare name pip resolves as a local archive on a suffix match -- `evil.tar.gz` -- before it considers whether the string looks like a path at all); `vcs url`; `direct url`; `option line`; `include` (a `-r`/`-c` the pure grammar classified but did not resolve -- the pyproject branch never resolves includes, so this reaches the manifest there); `include outside target`; `nested include`; `include unreadable`; `unparseable`.

hashes_stripped.description: True when at least one `--hash=` token was removed from a kept line. pip-audit does not need them, and one left in would impose `--require-hashes` semantics the generated file cannot satisfy.

truncated.description: True when the source manifest was larger than the adapter would read (1 MiB or 20,000 lines, whichever bit first), so lines beyond the bound were neither audited nor disclosed. The read is capped because this text is target-authored and lands in two published artifacts; the cap is stated rather than applied silently, which would be a second partial audit nobody was told about.

dropped_truncated.description: How many further dropped lines exist beyond the 200 listed in `dropped`. 0 when the list is complete. The rows are capped for the same reason the read is; the COUNT is always exact.

coverage.description: What this run actually did: which adapters produced usable output, which tools ran, verify-phase accounting, and the tool-policy posture.

adapters.description: Per output file: {status: ok|empty|noscan|failed, findings: int, reason?: str, file_coverage?: object}. file_coverage separates usable scanner output from complete file coverage: status complete|partial, parsed_files/unparsed_files/unavailable_files counts, bounded files [{file, reason}], files_omitted, and capabilities_unavailable. Partial captures keep their genuine findings and baseline eligibility; summary.coverage_certified is false with an explicit coverage_note. A failed file (0-byte, unparseable, or no registered adapter) is not counted as having run. noscan (#1335) = the adapter ran and produced a valid document but scanned zero files, so it gets no coverage credit.

tools_file_partial.description: Adapters with usable captures but incomplete file coverage, mapped to the same bounded file_coverage facts in adapters. Reasons: parse_error or typescript_parser_unavailable. Findings still gate; file gaps alone do not invalidate a baseline or change the finding-based gate. summary.coverage_certified is false.

tools_ran.description: Adapters whose run earns coverage credit (status ok or empty). Excludes noscan: an adapter that scanned zero files covered nothing (#1335).

build_executing_tools.description: Names of adapters from EXECUTES_TARGET_BUILD that ran this run (produced an output file), whether or not they emitted findings.

tool_policy_mode.description: Posture of the fan-out reviewer entries (panel_review/lens_sweep) derived from dispatch plans; scout/advisor posture is not recorded. "unknown" means no dispatch plan was found.

verdicts.description: Verify-phase accounting: verdicts that were dropped are otherwise stderr-only, and under strict gating a run whose verdicts all failed to match looks like a clean pass.

unanswered.description: Queued findings left without a verdict; null when no --verdicts-dir was supplied, i.e. not measured.

misrouted.description: #1475: verdict files that EXISTED for the cell they were written for but could not be bound to it -- the finding_id echo named a different finding, or none. Also counted in `unanswered` (the finding has no valid verdict either way), but the cause is the OPPOSITE of a missing dispatch: an advisor ran, adjudicated, and mislabelled its answer. Reported separately so the two are distinguishable without reading agent transcripts.

unloadable.description: Verdict files present on disk but un-loadable (corrupt/invalid JSON); their findings are left unverified. A non-zero count means verification evidence was lost, distinct from a verdict that was never generated (#938).

fan_out.description: Planned-vs-executed fan-out coverage derived at synthesis from the dispatch plan and the findings files on disk: {planned, executed, groups_complete, groups_partial}. null when no dispatch plan was present.

scout_profiles_seen.description: Scout profiles harvested; with scout_requested, distinguishes 'no scouts ran' (0) from 'scouts ran and requested no tools' (N>0 with []).

scout_requested.description: Union of tools requested across scout profiles.

out_of_scope.description: #441 reviewer scope disclosure: {checked, count, examples} of findings citing files outside their group's assigned list; null when no plan/group could be checked.

doc_policy.description: #487 planning-doc severity policy disclosure: {downgraded, examples}; null when redteam bypassed the policy.

divergence.description: Planned-vs-executed gaps: {panels: {name: {planned, executed}}, tools: {name: 'requested_absent'|'produced_unusable'|'requested_unavailable'|'produced_noscan'|'network_unavailable'}}. network_unavailable (safe egress could not be established), requested_absent (selected, no output) and produced_unusable (#1512: output produced but ingestion could not parse it) are lost required coverage and reach tools_absent, so they gate. requested_unavailable (scout asked for a tool the runner cannot run) and produced_noscan (#1335: ran but scanned zero files) are disclosure only and never gate.

cells.description: 5.0 (matrix Sec5.1) certifiable-coverage audit of the FLOOR cells: `{"missing_floor": [[group, domain], ...]}`. A floor (group, domain) cell that produced no findings file is lost required coverage, and a non-empty list is what forces the gate to INCONCLUSIVE. Scout-WIDENED domains are never audited here -- the floor is the contract -- and a floor domain the group explicitly excluded is netted out first.

reviewed.description: Optional measured completed review cells as sorted [group, DOMAIN] pairs, preserving exact group/chunk identity. Derived from ingested agent findings paths after malformed cells are removed; empty means measured with none completed, omission means unknown. Tool findings never establish agent-cell review. Disclosure only; missing_floor remains the coverage gate.

planned_pairs.description: Optional measured planned review cells as sorted [group, DOMAIN] pairs from coverage records' effective domains, preserving exact group/chunk identity. Published with reviewed when ingested-path and plan measurement exist; omission means unknown. An empty panel cell has zero findings with complete review only when every nonempty planned domain for that group/panel is reviewed. Disclosure only; coverage gates are unchanged.

tools_suppressed.description: #1578 (SEC-G2B): `{segment: count}` -- how many TOOL findings this run's ingest dropped for sitting under a conventional vendored-dependency directory (`vendor`, `node_modules`, `third_party`, `vendored`, `bower_components`, `.bundle`, `.yarn`), matched as a full path segment at any depth, keyed by the segment that matched. #1740 (ARC-F2A) widens the key vocabulary to EVERY rule that drops a finding on a directory NAME alone, because they rest on the same evidence: the vendored list above, a `venv`/`.venv`/`site-packages` segment with no `pyvenv.cfg` behind it (a marker-confirmed virtualenv is evidence rather than a name, is dropped silently and is not in this tally), and the reserved pseudo-segment `fixture-corpus` for the test-fixture prune. `ingest_tools.suppression_class` maps a key to its class (`vendored` / `virtualenv-by-name` / `fixture-corpus`), which is how the ingest's stderr note and `security_gate`'s verdict line group them; drops the OPERATOR asked for (`--tools-exclude` / `--exclude` globs) are counted as exclusions and never appear here. The exclusion earns its keep -- calibration-5/solidus: 592 of eslint-security's 623 messages were bundled jQuery under `vendor/` -- but it matches a NAME with no provenance behind it (no lockfile, no vendoring marker, no `.gitattributes linguist-vendored`), so a real vendored library and a payload parked at `app/vendor/patched_auth.rb` are the same event unless the drop is counted where an operator can see it. The loss is SINGLE-AXIS: `discovery.EXCLUDE_DIRS` does not hold these names, so the agentic panel still discovers, groups and reviews those files. The count is what was suppressed FROM THE GATE, which is not always what was suppressed from the body: #1701 gave the driver's own gate the treatment `security_gate.py --security redteam` already had, so under `--security redteam` a drop that clears the `--severity` floor and the delta / `gate_scope` filter is counted toward `summary.gate` and the health grade exactly as an un-suppressed finding of that severity would be, and moves out of this count into `tools_suppressed_gated`; what stays here under redteam is the part those two filters scoped out, plus -- #1578 owner ruling 2026-09-22, policy C -- the part the gate SAW and declined because it is neither CRITICAL nor secret-class (`tools_suppressed_not_gated` counts that second part on its own; it is a SUBSET of this one, not a third number beside it). So a redteam run with `--gate-scope on-diff`, a high `--severity` floor, or a tree full of bundled-library lint findings can still publish a non-zero segment -- still named, because the finding IS still withheld from `findings[]`. In `standard` mode the suppression stands for the gate too and the count is the full tally, printed beside the gate line as well. The MERGE GATE asks the same predicate -- `security_gate.py --security redteam` evaluates the CRITICAL and secret-class part of the suppressed set alongside the kept one, through the one definition `ingest_tools.gates_when_suppressed` -- but it composes the answer differently, on purpose. There, a policy-admitted finding BYPASSES `GATE_SEVERITIES`, a floor that module hard-codes and no operator chose, so a secret-class MEDIUM under `vendor/` blocks a merge. Here the same finding is counted in this key and then still meets `--fail-on`, which is operator POLICY in the same class as `--exclude` and as the `--severity` floor already applied to these candidates (#1701 F1) -- panopticon does not override an operator's flag. So this count means POLICY-ADMITTED, not necessarily verdict-moving: at `--fail-on high` a secret-class MEDIUM appears here and `summary.gate` still PASSes. `{}` means the ingest ran and dropped nothing, or that no tool ingest ran at all; repaired to these types at the read by `synth.repair.repair_tools_suppressed` (counts derive from scanner-reported paths) and bounded there to 200 segments of at most 200 characters.

tools_suppressed_gated.description: #1701: the other half of the `tools_suppressed` tally -- `{segment: count}` of TOOL findings that a directory-NAME exclusion withheld from `findings[]` and that THIS RUN'S GATE counted anyway (#1740: all three classes of it -- vendored, virtualenv-by-name, fixture-corpus). Non-empty only under `--security redteam`, where a finding may not be dropped on the strength of a conventional directory name -- and, since the #1578 owner ruling of 2026-09-22 (policy C), only where it is ALSO worth blocking a merge for: a CRITICAL, or a secret-class finding (a secret adapter such as gitleaks, or a credential CWE -- CWE-798/259/321/522). `ingest_tools.gates_when_suppressed` is the one definition, asked by this gate and by `security_gate.py` alike. What the rule declines is counted in `tools_suppressed_not_gated` and stays inside `tools_suppressed`. Those findings count toward `summary.gate`, `summary.risk_level`, `summary.gate_severities` and the health index exactly as un-suppressed findings of the same severity and location would, after the same `--severity` floor and the same delta / `gate_scope` filter, but they are NOT added to `findings[]` -- so a gate that FAILs on them shows no finding, and this count is the only thing in the artifact that explains it. Counted here means POLICY-ADMITTED, not necessarily verdict-moving: the driver's gate then still applies the operator's `--fail-on` floor to these findings, where `security_gate.py` lets a policy-admitted finding bypass its own hard-coded `GATE_SEVERITIES` -- see `tools_suppressed` for why the two compose differently on purpose -- so at `--fail-on high` a secret-class MEDIUM appears here while `summary.gate` still PASSes. Read it beside `tools_suppressed`: the two sum, per segment, to the number the ingest printed on stderr and the number `security_gate.py` prints beside its own verdict, which is the one-definition rule `ingest_tools.suppressed_counts` exists to keep. `{}` means this run's gate counted nothing suppressed -- the `standard`-mode answer, and also the redteam answer when the drops were scoped out by the diff or the severity floor. The suppressed findings are never sent through the verify round (they are not in the body to be queued), so unlike the rest of the gate population they are counted without an advisor verdict. That asymmetry was #1578's open policy question and it STANDS: option A (queue them for tool-verify) was rejected on dispatch cost, and policy C narrows which findings it applies to instead.
tools_suppressed_gated.$comment: Repaired to these types at the read by synth.repair.repair_tools_suppressed, like its sibling.

tools_suppressed_not_gated.description: #1578 (SEC-G2B), owner ruling 2026-09-22 -- policy C. `{segment: count}` of TOOL findings that a directory-NAME exclusion withheld from `findings[]`, that cleared this run's `--severity` floor and its delta / `gate_scope` filter, and that the redteam gate still did NOT count -- because they are neither CRITICAL nor secret-class. Non-empty only under `--security redteam`: in `standard` mode the suppression stands for the gate outright, policy C never runs, and the whole tally sits in `tools_suppressed`. A SUBSET of `tools_suppressed`, never a third number beside it: that key counts everything the gate did not take, and this one says how much of it this rule is responsible for rather than the floor or the diff. Published because the ruling trades a gate FAIL for silence unless the number is there: the objection policy C answers is that a vendor-heavy tree hard-FAILed a merge on unverified scanner noise (calibration-5/solidus: 592 of eslint-security's 623 messages were one rule firing on bundled jQuery under `vendor/`), and the cost of answering it is real findings the gate now lets past -- so an operator reading a PASS has to be able to see how many, and under which segment. `{}` means the rule declined nothing this run.
tools_suppressed_not_gated.$comment: Repaired to these types at the read by synth.repair.repair_tools_suppressed, like its two siblings.

globs.description: The path globs that scoped this run's tool ingest: the repository's committed top-level `exclude_paths:` (threaded by the driver as `--tools-exclude`, and to the scan as `run_tools --exclude`), or whatever an operator passed directly. Published even when a glob matched nothing this run -- the policy scoped the run either way, and a reader comparing two runs has to see it. Repaired at the read (`synth.repair.repair_tools_excluded`): a non-string or over-long glob is dropped rather than cut, because a cut glob is a different glob and would misstate the policy.

count.description: How many TOOL findings those globs dropped at ingest. Distinct from `tools_suppressed`/`tools_suppressed_gated` in kind, not just in number: a suppression is this system's own inference from a conventional DIRECTORY NAME, and under `--security redteam` the gate counts it anyway (#1578/#1740), while an exclusion is a decision the operator or the repository made about scope -- so these findings are counted, disclosed, and never gated in any mode.

tools_excluded.description: #1740 (ARC-F2A, fix round 2): the exclusion POLICY this run's tool ingest applied, and what it removed. `exclude_paths:` is authored by the repository under review and (since #1740) scopes the scanners, this report and the gate, so a committed `['**']` that empties the tool axis is a fact the ARTIFACT must carry -- it was visible only in `groups.json`, `tools-manifest.json` and an ingest stderr line nobody keeps. Stated on every report, `{"globs": [], "count": 0}` included: the field's absence must never be readable as `nothing was excluded`. `security_gate.py` prints the same two numbers beside its own verdict line.

test_inventory.description: #1638 P13: per REVIEW UNIT -- the root config's `groups:` entry, so a run-time `<name>_N` chunk answers as its parent -- whether the test inventory that unit's reviewers were shown could be believed: complete (it holds tests, or holds no code at all), empty (it holds code and no test, on either the `tests:` axis or in its own file list), or split (test files named after its modules are claimed by another unit). Recorded by the review phase as each prompt was rendered. An empty or split entry means a `TST` no-coverage claim from that unit may be a defect in the MATRIX, not in the target's test suite; run-13 published exactly that claim for a module whose 138 tests the same session had run green. No agent files a finding for it -- the state is driver-computed and published here. `{}` means this run did not measure it (a direct synthesize.py call), which is a different fact from every unit being complete.

repo.description: Which repository carried the setting: `.` for the review root, else the submodule's path relative to it.

key.description: The config key that was emptied, e.g. `filter.lfs.clean`. The VALUE is never published: it is a command line the reviewed tree authored.

git_drivers_suppressed.description: #2013: the TARGET's own Git driver commands this scan ran with EMPTIED. Every git call on a review target goes through a probe that refuses to run a command the reviewed tree configured (#1985/#2006); refusing such a target outright made a git-lfs (`git lfs install --local`) or git-crypt checkout unreviewable on every path that touches git, so the probe now overrides each `filter.*.clean/.process/.smudge`, `diff.external` and `diff.*.command/.textconv` it finds with `-c <key>=` (plus that driver's `required` flag, which would otherwise turn the emptied command into a hard error), proves each override took, and discloses the keys here. It changes what git COMPARES, not what any reviewer was shown (agents read the worktree; the probe never checks anything out): a clean filter is what makes the index blob equal the worktree, so paths under a suppressed driver compare as MODIFIED — dirtiness for them is unknown and a delta may include them. That is why this rides the artifact and not only the run manifest, and why a delta-scoped run over such a comparison cannot certify its coverage (see meta.integrity.delta_scope_suppressed_git_drivers). Stated on every report, `[]` included: the field's absence must never be readable as `the target configured none`. `[]` means no driver was emptied under this run's probe; it does NOT distinguish a run whose manifest predates this field, which the driver also threads as nothing (reachable only on a run resumed across that upgrade). Repaired at the read (`synth.repair.repair_git_drivers_suppressed`): the key half is repository-authored.

resume.description: Resume accounting for fan-out/verify phases; null on fresh full runs.

delta.description: Delta-review disclosure (#449): {base, base_source, base_commit, delta_start, delta_end, includes_uncommitted, files_changed, diff_context, on_diff_total, pre_existing_total}; null outside delta mode.

verify_matrix.description: P5 verify-matrix accounting: engaged (>= F_p) cell count and the engaged cells left unverified (which force gate INCONCLUSIVE).

host_capabilities.description: 5.2 surface 2 (#1344 F3b): the host posture this run VERIFIED, copied verbatim off `runs/<tag>/host-capabilities.json`. Documented in prose since #1344 and undescribed here until #1602 -- the drift the parity test (tests/test_schema_parity.py) now exists to prevent. Every field fails closed (`null`, `{}` for the maps) on an artifact that is absent, truncated or not a JSON object, so a malformed record reads as "nobody looked" rather than as a posture. The INNER values are described but not type-pinned on purpose: this subtree is copied verbatim out of a file under `.panopticon`, which a hostile target can pre-commit, and the posture is disclosure that explicitly does NOT gate (it moves no grade, no gate and no certification). Pinning types here would hand that target a way to make every run exit `artifact invalid` -- a junk posture must be readable AS junk, not a reason to throw the report away. The shape below is what panopticon's own probes write.

host.description: The host the posture was measured on (claude / codex / kimi / generic); null when no readable artifact named one.

schema_version.description: Version of the host-capabilities ARTIFACT's own format -- what a consumer diffing two runs needs before it may compare them at all. Normally an integer; deliberately UNTYPED here, with `probed_at` and the `capabilities` triple, for the reason in this section's description.

probed_at.description: When this posture was last ESTABLISHED (the record is rewritten when something an operator cares about moves, not on every probe), so the interval probed_at..end-of-run is one over which the enforcement posture held unbroken. Normally an ISO-8601 string. Distinct from meta.timestamp, which is synthesis time. Never defaulted: "nobody wrote down when" has to stay distinguishable from a measured moment.

capabilities.description: The artifact's capability map VERBATIM, one entry per capability name (tool_policy_enforced, read_scope_confined, artifact_write_guard, model_binding, usage_ledger), so the REASON survives into the report and two runs can be diffed rather than merely compared. `{}` means nothing was measured, which is a different fact from every capability being refuted.

state.description: `proven`, `refuted` or `unknown`, as written by the probe. `unknown` is NOT benign -- nobody looked -- and is treated exactly as `refuted` wherever posture is consumed; the two are kept apart because they have different remedies. Stated here rather than pinned as an enum, for the reason in this section's description.

by.description: Probe id that established the state (e.g. registered-shell-tools, read-guard-armed, kimi-usage-wire). `null` when no probe ran at all -- an `unknown` row carries its reason in `detail` and nothing in `by`.

detail.description: What the probe actually found, in the probe's own words -- the half of a disclosure that makes it a disclosure rather than a mood. Every agreeing probe's finding, joined.

cli_flags.description: D10 N3: the operational CLI facts ride BESIDE `capabilities`, never inside it, exactly as they do in the artifact -- a consumer diffing two postures must not read a flag that gates nothing as a capability that moved.

integrity.description: Run-integrity reconciliation driving certification: unexpected, duplicate, mislabeled, malformed, content-mismatched, empty, or invalid dispatch artifacts force gate INCONCLUSIVE — as does a fan-out snapshot that is corrupt (content_snapshot_unreadable) or owed-but-absent (content_snapshot_missing).

malformed_findings_files.description: #1513: findings files that violate the findings contract, as [{file, cell: [group, domain]|null, defects: [{index, reason}]}]. A stamped cell whose findings list holds a non-object is not a completed clean review; these fail the gate closed and their cells are netted out of the floor audit. Dropped source evidence used to exist only on stderr.

cross_domain_findings.description: #calibration-4: findings filed under a domain other than their cell's -- REPORTED, never gating. A reviewer that files a TST finding from an ARC cell has stepped outside its lane, which is a real signal about panel discipline and about catalog gaps (most are `<DOM>-X0X`), but it is evidence about the REVIEW, not about whether the artifacts on disk can be trusted. Treating it as an integrity failure once sank certification on a run whose file integrity was perfect.

ack_stale.description: #493 R2: the on-disk ack did not hash-match any dispatch plan; reported false above when stale.

content_hashes_checked.description: #493 R4: findings files verified against the fan-out snapshot; null = no snapshot (not measured).

content_snapshot_unreadable.description: The fan-out snapshot EXISTS but is corrupt/empty — a tamper signal, not a missing snapshot. Fails the gate closed.

content_snapshot_missing.description: #1511/#1208: the run's dispatch plan declares review cells, so a snapshot was OWED, and none is present — a deleted baseline. Fails the gate closed. False on a run that owes nothing (no driver plan), which keeps the benign 'not measured' reading.

invalid_verify_queue.description: A present verify-queue artifact could not be parsed or had no entries list; forces INCONCLUSIVE.

tools_manifest_invalid.description: #1644: this run's tools-manifest.json EXISTS and could not be read (unreadable, not JSON, or not a JSON object) — the reason, else null. Corruption is not absence: with the runner's selected set unknown, `tools_absent` cannot be computed at all, so the report claims none and `summary.coverage_certified` is false with `coverage_note` saying why. It does NOT move `summary.gate`, which reports what the findings say — the certification/gate distinction. A manifest that parses to an object with malformed FIELDS is a different case, repaired at the read (see meta.tools.sanitized / network) and never recorded here.

delta_scope_suppressed_git_drivers.description: #2013 fix round 1: the suppressed target Git driver keys that scoped this run's DELTA, else null. Emptying a `filter.*.clean` removes the equality it created between the index blob and the worktree, so git then compares raw worktree bytes against a filtered blob and paths under a suppressed driver compare as MODIFIED (measured: index `ptr payload`, worktree `BIG payload`, plain `git status` clean, the probe's `status` reporting the path modified). On a full-repo scan that costs `target_dirty` in the run manifest and nothing the findings depend on, so `meta.coverage.git_drivers_suppressed` discloses it and certification is unaffected. On a delta-scoped run (`--changes`, or any diff-hunks map with a base: `--scope-changed` / `--pr`) the inflated comparison CHOSE the reviewed file set and the on-diff gate's scope, so this caveat is named, `summary.coverage_certified` is false and `coverage_note` says why. Like every other reason in this section it forces `summary.gate` to INCONCLUSIVE through `integrity_ok`, never past a FAIL. Null means this run was not delta-scoped, or suppressed nothing — never `not measured`.

dispatch_plan_missing.description: SEC-377944137/#1832: the run manifest's own `driver_plan` stamp says this run WROTE a dispatch plan, and no dispatch-plan file is present at synthesis — deleted evidence. Fails the gate closed. #1208's reading of an owed-but-absent fan-out snapshot, applied to the file that decides whether the snapshot is owed at all: deleting the plan silenced the planned-vs-ingested reconciliation, the out_file-collision check, the snapshot obligation and the fan-out accounting at once, so one more `rm` turned a DETECTED findings substitution back into a clean run. The driver no longer re-creates either artifact once it has stamped it, so the absence is reported rather than repaired. False on a run that never wrote a plan (a direct synthesize.py call over hand-collected findings, a target with no declared cells, or a run resumed across the upgrade that added the stamp), which keeps the benign 'not measured' reading every other key here has.

dispatch_plan_mismatched.description: SEC-377944137/#1832: a dispatch plan IS present and parses, but its canonical content does not hash to the `driver_plan` stamp the run manifest recorded when the driver wrote it — substituted evidence. Fails the gate closed. Replacing the plan is the same erasure as deleting it and cheaper: a narrower plan declares fewer cells, so the planned-vs-ingested reconciliation has less to miss and the snapshot obligation shrinks. An UNREADABLE plan is not counted here (the loader reports it as invalid_dispatch_plans; one fault, one key). False when the stamp carries no hash or the run never wrote a plan.

cost.description: Dispatch ledger for the run, derived from artifacts (scout profiles, dispatch plans, verify queue). The 4.x cost baseline the 5.x economics work keys on.

tokens.description: Host-reported token usage, read verbatim from <run_dir>/usage.json when the host writes it (#run10 D4). Null when it does not -- never estimated from the dispatch counts.

config.description: #1681 Plan 2 (spec §4): the reviewed repository's own `settings:` section, and what this run did with it. `requested` is what the committed config asked for, verbatim; `effective` is what the trust classes let through (a grain value after its clamp, a gate value at least as strict as panopticon's default); `refused` and `clamped` say what did not survive and why; `disclosures` is the same in prose, as the terminal summary prints it. The maps' KEYS and VALUES come from a target-authored file and are deliberately not type-pinned, for meta.host_capabilities' reason -- this is disclosure that gates nothing, and a junk config must be readable as junk rather than a way to make the report fail its own schema. Empty maps and lists mean the config asked for nothing, which is a measurement, not an absence.

overall_grade.description: Letter banded over summary.health.score: S=100, A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F>=26, X below. S is reachable ONLY at exactly 100 (no gate-eligible weighted defect). Supersedes the max-severity rollup, which saturated -- one HIGH anywhere was a D at any codebase size. null when health is unmeasurable (no readable reviewed LoC) or when coverage is incomplete, in which case provisional_grade carries the letter.

provisional_grade.description: The letter overall_grade would have carried, held back because coverage did not complete. Same bands.

stats_population.description: Which finding population summary.stats counts. 'active' = non-rejected findings (== findings[]).

gate_severities.description: The gate's reach across the severity distribution. `in_play` = severities at or above --fail-on (any finding there would FAIL); `contributing` = the subset that actually holds a GATE-ELIGIBLE finding, i.e. what the FAIL is made of. Derived from the gate-eligible set, NOT from summary.stats (which counts the ACTIVE set, including unverified findings that cannot gate) -- so `contributing` is non-empty if and only if gate == FAIL. All three fields are empty/null when no --fail-on was given.

fail_on.description: The threshold in force, uppercased; null when no --fail-on was given or it was unrecognised.

in_play.description: Severities at or above the threshold, worst first.

contributing.description: The in-play severities holding at least one gate-eligible finding.

evidence_stats_population.description: Which finding population summary.evidence_stats counts. 'all' = active + discarded (== findings[] + discarded_claims[]).

counts.description: #1059: reconcilable finding-population totals so the two histograms above are never ambiguous. active == len(findings[]); discarded == len(discarded_claims[]); total == active + discarded.

health.description: #1146: secondary size-aware health index reported ALONGSIDE the max-severity letter (never touches the gate or the letter). score = 100 * total_loc / (total_loc + weighted_defect) -- a 0-100 scale where HIGHER is healthier and 100 means no gate-eligible weighted defect; null ONLY when both inputs are 0 (nothing reviewed). Population is the gate-eligible set, same as the letter. Supersedes total_loc / weighted_defect, which ran backwards, was unbounded above, and returned null for a CLEAN repo; both inputs are still emitted, so any report -- including one written under the old formula -- can be recomputed under either.

score.description: 0-100, higher is healthier. null only when total_loc and weighted_defect are both 0.

total_loc.description: Non-blank lines across the unique reviewed files (the numerator).

weighted_defect.description: Sum over gate-eligible findings of weight[severity] * lines-spanned.

weights.description: Severity weights used: info 0, low 1, medium 5, high 25, critical 125.

formula.description: The exact expression used to compute `score`, so a report is self-describing across formula changes.

delta.description: Delta gate summary: on-diff and pre-existing per-severity counts; null outside delta mode.

panel_grades.description: Per-panel A-F, still the MAX-SEVERITY rollup and deliberately not health-banded: health needs lines of code, and LoC is not attributable per panel (one file feeds several). Do not read these on the same scale as summary.overall_grade.

short_title.description: The title trimmed to issue-title length, derived by findings normalization on EVERY finding (equal to `title` when it already fits). Tool messages are sometimes whole remediation paragraphs; the issue filer, the X0X candidate builder and the strain report all read this and keep the full text in the body.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity of the CLAIM (panel/category/file/title-derived), the same identity the verify queue keys a verdict on. Exported so a consumer can bind a finding across runs and across the queue. KNOWN DIVERGENCE: the queue disambiguates a collision with a `-<n>` suffix that never appears here, so a fingerprint -> queue_id lookup is ambiguous for a colliding pair.

delta.description: #449 on-diff classification against the run's diff-hunks.json, stamped on every finding in delta mode and absent outside it. `on_diff` fails OPEN (true) where the file changed but the finding carries no line, so a delta gate never silently drops a claim it could not place.

location.description: #1522: a location, if present, identifies a FILE. line_start is optional -- a whole-file finding (missing header, bad config) is legitimate and must not have a line number invented for it. A finding with no locus at all (a repo-wide catalog- or coverage-gap finding) carries no location key at all; `location` is not in the finding-level required list.

missing_evidence.description: Present with status `backup_scope_limited` (#1638 P16): the files the backup advisor said it was not granted. The primary CONFIRMED stands and the report names what the second opinion could not see, instead of implying it looked and could not tell.

advisor_code.description: The OCRDb code the verify advisor independently landed on, recorded ONLY when it differs from the finding's own `code`. Never applied — the advisor is a second opinion, not an authority on the catalog, so re-coding on one opinion is refused for the same reason severity is untouched. Its presence is the catalog-STRAIN flag: the panel filed one code and an independent re-read preferred another. A value ending `-X0X` means the advisor judged the panel's real code a mis-fit; an `-X0X` finding whose advisor_code is a real code means the reverse.
